hypothesis: One legal collision-preserving dependency template completely separates a same-body self-join-free combined-query pair when their counted-variable closures differ.
hypothesis_novelty_result: NULL: standard FD projection bijection and Armstrong two-tuple nonimplication construction cover the mechanism

fragment.schema: set-valued relations; exactly one nonempty possibly composite PK per table; every column NOT NULL; complete-PK FKs only; directed FK graph acyclic and underlying undirected simple graph a forest; no other constraints
fragment.body: one common nonempty safe relational conjunction B with identical variable naming; each predicate occurs at most once; variables only; equalities represented by repeated variables; explicitly FK-closed with matching variable tuples
fragment.queries: same ordered head H; different counted-variable sets M,N disjoint from H; all other variables existential; multiplicity equals count of projected satisfying assignments
fragment.strictness_caution: Contains cases outside key-anchorability; does not contain the entire FewRows fragment
fragment.domain_and_typing: Every relation position and variable uses one common infinite opaque equality domain. Queries are well typed. No coercions, finite-width SQL types, enumerations, NULL, or additional domain constraints are admitted. Finite databases over this infinite domain only.
fragment.input_representation: Explicit integer IDs; M and N each encoded as duplicate-free subsets of body variables. Any noncompact or duplicate representation has its actual encoded read length charged separately.

theorem.fd_system: For each atom A, PK-variable-set K_A -> vars(A)
theorem.equivalence_iff: closure(H union M) = closure(H union N)
theorem.inequivalence_direction: Pick m in M minus closure(H union N), exchanging M,N if needed
theorem.template: Let C=closure(H union N). Let S be the component containing m in the atom-incidence hypergraph induced on V minus C. Freeze variables outside S; synchronously assign n pairwise tagged values to all variables of S; materialize each atom under every shared index.
theorem.legal_for: all positive integers n, only under the explicit common infinite opaque equality-domain and well-typed fragment
theorem.separation: exactly n versus 1 copies of the fixed head tuple
theorem.exact_row_formula: a + (n-1)*s, where s is the number of atoms intersecting S
theorem.construction_cost: O(S+L+h+v) word operations for a fixed T(2) with compact M,N: S full schema encoding including unused tables/columns and every constraint, L explicit body variable occurrences, h complete ordered head length including repeated positions, v distinct body variables. More generally add actual counted-set encoding length j, O(S+L+h+j+v).
theorem.search_cost: no equality-type enumeration, no database enumeration, no solver, no PIT; closure comparison and one component choice
theorem.assignment_safety: Self-join-freeness enforces each variable's local tagged domain; one varying component enforces one shared index, hence exactly n full satisfying assignments.
theorem.fk_caution: Input includes already FK-closed body; no hidden chase-size claim
theorem.evaluation_caution: Linear exact output derivation holds for this proven template, not generic SQL evaluation
theorem.output_bit_cost: O(L log(v+1)) concerns only witness tagged data cells. Complete delivery and input cost additionally charge schema/table identifiers, head/certificate materialization, encoded input and parsing. No generic SQL evaluator or implicit chase cost claim.

counterexamples.dropping_self_join_free: R(x,y) AND R(y,x), full-tuple PK, count x vs count y: closures differ but queries always equivalent; naive two-index template yields 3 vs 3
counterexamples.dropping_aligned_common_body: R(k,x,y) vs R(k,y,x), key k, count x on both: identical FDs and closure{x}, but R={(1,7,8),(2,7,9)} gives 1 vs 2. Any body alignment must transport the counted set.
counterexamples.first_failed_proof_step: The two count projections no longer originate from one common satisfying-assignment relation
counterexamples.set_equivalent_boundary_lemma: Under all the other pure-variable, self-join-free, explicitly FK-closed restrictions, set-equivalent bodies must be head-preserving renaming-isomorphic. Each canonical DB is already legal and yields a reverse homomorphism; self-join-free endomorphisms fix every positional variable, so the maps are inverses. Transport counted sets along the isomorphism before closure comparison.
counterexamples.boundary_lemma_novelty: NULL: standard canonical-database set-containment specialization, not a new mechanism or a fixture-scope change
